metadata.note: The Des Moines Valley line, Keokuk - Des Moines up the Des Moines River valley, in its three operating eras: the Keokuk, Fort Des Moines & Minnesota / Des Moines Valley Rail Road (1857-1873, drawn stage by stage as it was built), the Keokuk & Des Moines Railway (1874-1878), and the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific under lease from 1 Oct 1878; plus the 1875 Keosauqua North & South and the Rock Island's 1880 Keosauqua Branch. Drawn from research/branches/keokuk_and_des_moines_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-11-04; before this layer no feature drew this line in any era. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4 splits: DMV -> K&DM at the 1873/1874 boundary (foreclosure 10 Nov 1873, conveyance 12 Feb 1874) and K&DM -> Rock Island at the 1878 lease; the 1864 KFDM&M -> DMV renaming and the 1924/1948 corporate mergers are not splits. Rock Island features reuse the company string and colour of crip-chicago-omaha in chicago_rock_island_pacific.geojson; the Des Moines Valley, K&DM and Keosauqua N&S colours are new and used by no other company. Rock Island-era trains used the RI's own Washington - Knoxville line for Evans - Oskaloosa and the RI Chicago - Omaha main line for Altoona - Des Moines; both borrowed stretches are drawn in RI colour and labelled in geometry_quality.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), Rock Island Tables 3 and 23 and General Index of Stations - research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt in the site repo  (OG52)
metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) for lifted grades, traced with opstrace.py: Dijkstra over all railway ways, ways tagged old_railway_operator=CRI&P costed 1x, untagged rail 1.25x, cycleways 3x and any other named operator 12x; waypoints are the report's station towns (Nominatim, each geocode's type checked; Keokuk pinned to the Union Depot), snapped by a dynamic program; each leg confined to a corridor round its chord, and a leg longer than 1.6x its chord would have been drawn as a labelled straight line (none was); simplified at 8 m, reversals trimmed.
not_yet_sourced: Rock Island Keokuk - Oskaloosa (crip-keokuk-oskaloosa): [OPEN] end - 1948 is the last confirmed year (Oct 1948 mixed, KUD); the Feb 1952 Guide index suggests the mixed was still listed in Sept 1951 but no times survive. Actual end needs an Iowa Commerce Commission discontinuance order, a 'last train' newspaper story or a 1950s RI timetable.

Rock Island Evans - Des Moines (crip-evans-des-moines): [OPEN] end - 1942 is the last confirmed year (motor train 474/475, CRF); the end is probably between 1942 and 1951. Annals of Iowa 41:1 (1971) on Iowa passenger decline is the best next source.
Rock Island Keosauqua Branch (crip-keosauqua-branch): [ANCHOR] [OPEN] - only 1880 is proven; later years (probably to 1948-51) unconfirmed. Ownership (K&DM or RI) not established.
Keosauqua North and South (kns-mount-zion-keosauqua): [ANCHOR] 1875 only, single source (PITTMAN); whether it ran a scheduled passenger service at all is unclear.
Rock Island 1878-1948 continuity: anchors only at 1878, 1880, 1891, 1942 and 1948; a discontinuance and reinstatement in between would not show.
Ottumwa opening year: 1860 (Andreas 1875, MARVIG) vs a hint of 1859 for Ashland (REDDICK) - 1859 rejected as unproven.
Pella - Monroe 1865 rests on MARVIG alone, no month.
Nov 1873 - Feb 1874: who operated trains between the foreclosure sale and the conveyance to the K&DM.
Track gauge in 1857: Lanman (via REDDICK) says narrow gauge; ICC and others imply standard. Does not affect drawn years.
Line length Beacon - Evans: the trace (3.6 mi, matching MARVIG's 23 mi for Eddyville - Pella) conflicts with FOWLER's mileposts (Beacon 100, Evans 108).
Whether the Des Moines Valley's own 1866 line into Des Moines followed the later Rock Island main line from Altoona; FOWLER notes a 'former route until c.1955' there.
The Eldon historical marker's undated 'shortened Eldon - Ottumwa' doodlebug run (unread).
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.
branches_deliberately_omitted: Des Moines Valley northern line Des Moines - Fort Dodge (built c.1869-70): its DMV-run passenger years were not researched; FOWLER has only 1875 (Des Moines & Fort Dodge era) listings. The D&FD era is already drawn in minneapolis_and_st_louis_railway.geojson. A DMV feature needs a positive source first.
Bentonsport - Rock Creek 1857/58-1860: track reached Rock Creek before the two-year halt, but passenger trains there are not established; drawn from 1860 with the Bentonsport - Ottumwa feature.
Rock Island passenger years after the [OPEN] ends (1948 Keokuk - Oskaloosa, 1942 Evans - Des Moines, 1880 Keosauqua) - unconfirmed, not drawn.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Freight after the last confirmed passenger years (Keokuk - Oskaloosa to the 1975-80 period; Oskaloosa - Des Moines after the motor train), the post-1980 Iowa Interstate remnants (Des Moines - Altoona to 1986, Pella - Otley to 1998, Otley - Prairie City to 2000, Prairie City - Mitchellville to 2014) and the Keokuk Junction Railway stub at Keokuk are freight only and not drawn (Rule 1).
metadata.horsecar_audit: No animal traction: steam from June 1857; the 1875 Keosauqua North & South used 'two engines'. Nothing trimmed.

segments.note: First stage, down the Des Moines River valley via Sand Prairie, Croton, Farmington and Bonaparte. Trains reached Farmington for the celebration of 10 June 1857, Bonaparte 15 July and Bentonsport by 4 Aug 1857 (PITTMAN). Track went on to Rock Creek in 1857-58 and then halted two years, but passenger trains beyond Bentonsport before Sept 1860 are not established, so Bentonsport is drawn as the railhead. Steam from the start; Lanman's 'narrow gauge line laid without ballast' (via REDDICK) conflicts with ICC and the other sources, which treat the road as standard gauge - recorded, not resolved. Operated by the Keokuk, Fort Des Moines & Minnesota Rail Road, renamed the Des Moines Valley Rail Road at the end of 1864 (MARVIG) - one company, one colour. Its Keokuk - Des Moines line was sold at foreclosure 10 Nov 1873 and conveyed to the Keokuk & Des Moines Railway 12 Feb 1874 (ICC); the K&DM's own feature continues from 1874. Who ran trains between the sale and the conveyance is not recorded (report UNRESOLVED 6). headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no source gives a train count for these years.

segments.note: Report blocks [2] and [3], one feature because both start in 1860. Bentonsport - The Summit (Mount Zion) - Independent (Selma from 1882): 'the first train arrived [at The Summit] September 14, 1860. By late September that year, trains were running as far as Independence (now Selma)' (PITTMAN; Lanman via REDDICK gives the same day). This is the stretch that bypassed Keosauqua, climbing from Rock Creek to The Summit 4 mi north of the town. Selma - Ashland (near later Eldon) - Alpine - Ottumwa: completed to Ottumwa in 1860 (Andreas 1875 atlas via REDDICK; MARVIG 'by the end of 1860'); the month is not found, and 1861 is the first year certainly served end to end. REDDICK's hint of 1859 for Ashland is rejected as unproven and inconsistent with the Sept 1860 arrival at The Summit east of it. Eldon did not exist yet (founded at the Chicago & South Western crossing, first train 28 Oct 1870). FOWLER's 1868 and 1870 Guide listings of Independent, Ashland and Alpine are DMV-era passenger anchors. Operated by the Keokuk, Fort Des Moines & Minnesota Rail Road, renamed the Des Moines Valley Rail Road at the end of 1864 (MARVIG) - one company, one colour. Its Keokuk - Des Moines line was sold at foreclosure 10 Nov 1873 and conveyed to the Keokuk & Des Moines Railway 12 Feb 1874 (ICC); the K&DM's own feature continues from 1874. Who ran trains between the sale and the conveyance is not recorded (report UNRESOLVED 6). headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no source gives a train count for these years.

FOWLER's 'Des Moines (DMV) 1868G' is an 1868 Guide listing of the DMV's own terminus. The DMV's northern extension Des Moines - Fort Dodge is NOT drawn here (see metadata). segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1875 is the single proven year. The Keosauqua North & South Railroad (inc. 25 June 1873, later merged into the Keosauqua, St. Louis & Minnesota) was a SEPARATE company from the K&DM, built to give Keosauqua the rail link the Des Moines Valley had bypassed. Finished May 1875, it opened with an excursion carrying crowds on flatcars and one ex-canal dump car fitted with a canvas top as a 'passenger' car, worked by 'two engines' (steam, not animal); it 'fell into disuse within a few months after its completion' and its track was mostly lifted in 1879 (PITTMAN). Whether those few months were a scheduled passenger service or only the excursion plus occasional riders is unclear. Service certainly did not run beyond 1875 on any evidence found, and no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor. headway_min is a placeholder ESTIMATE; no schedule is known.

segments.note: Report blocks [9]-[10]: Keokuk - Bonaparte - Bentonsport - Mount Zion - Douds - Selma - Eldon - Ottumwa - Eddyville - Beacon - Evans, then the Rock Island's Washington - Knoxville line into Oskaloosa. Starts with the lease, in effect 1 Oct 1878 (ICC). [OPEN] END: 1948 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - the October 1948 Rock Island public timetable shows a Keokuk - Oskaloosa mixed train, one each way (KUD reproduces the schedule). The Feb 1952 Official Guide's index lists Keosauqua, Douds, Sand Prairie and Farmington under Rock Island Table 3 with no freight dagger, which suggests the mixed was still listed on 30 Sept 1951, but no times survive and the 'Mixed Service only' text cannot be tied to Table 3 with certainty, so 1951 is supporting evidence only and is NOT drawn. No source dates when passenger service actually stopped - do not extend without evidence. Continuity 1878-1948 rests on anchors at 1878, 1880, 1891 (Rock Island among Keokuk's passenger roads, KUD), 1942 and 1948; a discontinuance in between would not show. The 1942 Des Moines - Eldon motor train also served Eldon - Evans. Do NOT use 1967 - that is the end of the Burlington-Rock Island Zephyr Rocket, which reached Keokuk on CB&Q track, not on this line. Freight continued afterwards: Farmington - Keokuk 'temporarily out of service' by the Rock Island's last employee timetable (final movement reported 21 May 1975, RockIslandLines forum, unverified) and the line abandoned in the 1980 Rock Island liquidation (MARVIG). Operated by the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific under the K&DM lease from 1 Oct 1878 (ICC). The K&DM's corporate merger into the St. Paul & Kansas City Short Line (1924) and that company's merger into the Rock Island (1948) changed no operator and are not splits. headway_min is an ESTIMATE for the earlier decades; by 1948 the service was a single mixed train each way.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] 1880 is the single proven year, and service certainly ran on beyond it. The Rock Island rebuilt the abandoned Keosauqua North & South grade to standard gauge, drove the last spike Saturday 25 Sept 1880, 'ran the first passenger train into Keosauqua on Sept. 29, 1880', and ran a Keosauqua - Keokuk excursion 5 Oct 1880 (PITTMAN). Nothing later is CONFIRMED: the Feb 1952 Guide carries Keosauqua at mile 50 in Rock Island Table 3 (Mount Zion arr 46, Keosauqua arr/lve 50 - trains ran in and backed out) with no freight dagger in the index, so the Keokuk mixed probably still detoured into Keosauqua in Sept 1951, but no times survive; whether the Oct 1948 mixed called at Keosauqua was not established. PITTMAN's 'ever since that date Keosauqua has had railroad connection' is about rail, not passengers. Do not widen this anchor without a source; confirming Keosauqua in the 1948 schedule would justify 1880-1948 [OPEN]. Whether the branch was K&DM- or RI-owned is not established; the Rock Island built and ran it. headway_min is a placeholder ESTIMATE.
